component.name: Klia Store
component.summary: Browse, install and manage your Flatpak applications

description.p: Klia Store is a modern, fast application store built specifically for managing Flatpak applications on Linux. Beyond browsing and installing apps, it gives you tools to keep your system organized and under control.
Features:

ul.li: Browse, install and update Flatpak applications, all from one place
Back up and restore your installed applications, including their data and runtimes
Visualize your installed apps and their permissions (storage, camera, file access) in an interactive view
Audit installed apps by verifying their source manifest against Flathub, helping protect against supply-chain tampering
Review requested permissions and a risk assessment before installing a local .flatpak file
Available in multiple languages, with automatic detection of your system language

description.p: Klia Store now also shows the applications you installed from .deb packages. A source selector in My Apps switches between your Flatpak apps and your Debian packages, and every .deb application is listed with its real name, version and icon.

Those .deb applications can be uninstalled from the store. Before removing anything it lists every package that would be deleted, and it refuses to continue when the removal would drag along essential system packages or your desktop meta-package; the removal itself is confirmed with the desktop's own authentication prompt.
The About dialog was rebuilt around the project home page and the updates channel, and now includes a Contributors section that credits the people who worked on the project.

Language detection was fixed on Linux: the store now reads the language configured in your system instead of relying on the browser engine, so a session that only sets LANG no longer resolves to English. Japanese is now a selectable language, and the Chinese translation was brought in line with the English one.
Multiple bug fixes and stability improvements across the app.

Fixed the Flathub package, which was still being built against the previous GNOME platform even though the app itself had already moved on. The Flatpak version now really runs on GNOME 51, the same platform the other packages use.
The Flatpak and .deb packages are now built with the Node.js 24 long-term-support toolchain, instead of the older Node.js 20 line that no longer receives security updates.

Project dependencies were brought up to date (React 19.3, Vite 7.3, Material UI 7.3, TanStack Query 5.104, Tauri plugins). All packages now ship the same library versions, and the security advisories reported by npm audit are gone.
Klia Transcription is now the featured app on the Home screen, tagged as Beta: local call transcription with speaker separation and on-device summaries.

Klia Store now works local-first. If you lose your connection, the store keeps showing the content you already had instead of an error, and a yellow indicator in the title bar tells you that you are offline.
Installing an app or updating it while offline now shows a clear message, instead of a security warning you could not do anything about.
Updated to the GNOME 51 runtime, so Klia Store runs on the latest platform libraries.
Multiple bug fixes and stability improvements across the app.
Klia Store now correctly tells apart apps installed from Flathub versus apps installed from a GitHub release, and shows the source next to installed apps.
Fixed an issue where an app's available update could be detected but then get updated from the wrong source, or keep showing as "update available" forever after already being updated.
Fixed an issue where installing or updating Klia Kompress from Klia Store could fail with a file-not-found error.
Optimization pack: Klia Store now uses noticeably less RAM while running. You shouldn't notice any change in how the app looks or behaves — just a lighter footprint on your system.
Fixed an issue where installing a .flatpak file by double-clicking it could fail with a file-not-found error when Klia Store is running as a sandboxed Flatpak app.
Installing a .flatpak file by opening it directly now updates the app's status right away, so it correctly shows as installed without needing to restart Klia Store.
General performance improvements across the app: faster loading of the Home screen, quicker app searches, and a smaller, more efficient install.
Improved stability: the app is now more resilient if something goes wrong during an installation, avoiding unexpected crashes.
